newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola losses limited on CWB output estimate.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola losses limited on CWB output estimate.

text.p: WCE canola futures traded down with losses limited by a bullish Canadian Wheat Board Prairie oilseed production estimate, traders said.

"The Wheat Board's figures are holding us up. Chicago beans are down eight cents and we're only down $1.00," a trader said. XCan sold November down to $438.10 as crushers, commercials and locals bought between $438.50 and $438.10, traders said.
Japan bought 2,000 tonnes of canola, sources said.
November canola fell $1.10 to $438.40 at 1100 CDT. The CWB forecast canola output at 4.85 million tonnes and flax at 810,000 tonnes versus StatsCan's 5.29 and 850,000 for each.
October flax rose $0.70 to $396.50, November up $0.80 to $372.30 on commercial buying and rumoured export demand.

October feed wheat lost $2.70 to $206.50, December down $2.20 to $190.50 on commercial, commission profit taking. Oct-Mar spread at $22 on concerns of not enough railcar allocation to move feed wheat to the Thunder Bay pricing point after a rumored large CWB export program to China. Oct-May at $1, Dec-May at $6. December oats fell US$3 to US$130.
November western barley lost $0.90 to $149.20, February down $1.20 to $152.90 on hedge pressure. Nov-Feb at $3.50.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
